name: Candela laser
summary: Brand name for a family of clinic lasers (hair, tattoo, vascular, pigment); evidence exists per device, not for the brand as a whole.
lead: Candela is the name of a manufacturer of aesthetic laser systems, and in looksmaxxing discussion "Candela laser" refers to the clinic platforms sold under that brand rather than a single machine. Registered studies name its products including the GentleMax Pro (alexandrite plus Nd:YAG), a 1064-nm Nd:YAG skin-tightening system, a pulsed-dye (595 nm) laser and the PicoWay picosecond system.

name: Lumecca IPL
summary: InMode's high-intensity IPL for facial pigment and redness; supporting studies are small and IPL itself is an established category.
lead: Lumecca is a high-intensity intense pulsed light (IPL) device made by InMode, used in clinics for facial pigment and redness. IPL is not a laser: a xenon flashlamp emits broad-spectrum, non-coherent light, and filters select which light-absorbing targets (melanin or haemoglobin) are heated.

name: Sciton BBL / Moxi / Halo
summary: Sciton's IPL, 1927-nm fractional and hybrid fractional laser treatments for skin tone and texture; supporting studies are small.
lead: BBL, Moxi and Halo are treatments performed on laser and light platforms made by Sciton. BBL (BroadBand Light) is an intense pulsed light treatment, Moxi is a fractionated 1927-nm laser, and Halo is a dual-wavelength 2940/1470-nm hybrid fractional laser, as described by the titles of registered studies. They are used for photoaging, pigment, redness, texture and scars, and are sometimes combined in one session.

name: Moxi laser
summary: Sciton's light fractional 1927-nm laser for pigment and sun damage; only small studies exist.
lead: Moxi is a light fractional laser treatment from Sciton that uses a 1927-nm wavelength, as indicated by registered studies describing a fractionated 1927-nm laser and a trial combining BBL, Moxi (fractionated 1927) and Halo. It is used in clinics for pigmentation, sun damage and skin texture.

name: Excel V laser
summary: Cutera's 532 nm plus 1064 nm clinic laser for redness, vessels and pigment; supporting studies are small.
lead: Excel V is a vascular and pigment laser made by Cutera. It combines a 532-nm green laser (KTP-type, frequency-doubled Nd:YAG) with a 1064-nm Nd:YAG, and is used in clinics for redness, visible blood vessels, port-wine stains and pigment such as lentigines.

name: Laser genesis
summary: A gentle 1064-nm Nd:YAG laser facial treatment marketed for tone and redness; published appearance evidence is very thin.
lead: Laser Genesis is the name of a non-ablative skin treatment that uses a long-pulsed 1064-nm neodymium-doped yttrium aluminium garnet (Nd:YAG) laser at low energy. It is marketed for improving skin tone, redness and fine texture and is often described as a gentle, low-downtime option. A split-face trial refers to it as the 1064-nm long-pulsed Nd:YAG laser known as Laser Genesis .

name: Vbeam Perfecta
summary: Candela's 595 nm pulsed dye laser, a clinic mainstay for redness and vascular lesions; cosmetic-only evidence is thin.
lead: Vbeam Perfecta is a pulsed dye laser (PDL) system made by Candela that emits yellow light at 595 nm, a wavelength absorbed by hemoglobin. It is used in dermatology for vascular lesions such as port-wine stains, hemangiomas, facial telangiectasias and rosacea-related redness, and some practices offer it for scars and general facial redness .

name: Morpheus8 Burst
summary: The deeper Burst-mode RF microneedling setting of InMode's Morpheus8; little independent evidence exists for it specifically.
lead: Morpheus8 Burst refers to the Burst mode and deeper attachments of the Morpheus8 radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system from InMode, which uses insulated microneedles to deliver bipolar RF energy into the dermis and subdermal tissue . It is marketed for skin laxity, texture and mild fat remodeling.

name: Morpheus8 Body
summary: InMode's RF microneedling for larger body areas; evidence is limited to practice reports and one small registered study.
lead: Morpheus8 Body is the body-treatment version of InMode's Morpheus8 fractional radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system, used on areas such as the abdomen, arms and thighs for skin laxity and texture .

name: Fractora RF
summary: InMode's fractional RF pin handpiece, the forerunner of Morpheus8, studied for laxity and acne scars in small, mostly early studies.
lead: Fractora is a fractional bipolar radiofrequency (RF) microneedling-type handpiece from InMode, the platform that was later modified into Morpheus8 . It delivers RF energy through arrays of pins into the skin and has been studied for skin laxity, acne scars and oil production .

name: Profound RF
summary: Clinic-based radiofrequency microneedling system aimed at skin laxity, wrinkles and scars; documented mainly in registered device studies.
lead: Profound is a radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system used in aesthetic medicine. It combines needle insertion into the skin with RF energy delivered at depth, and is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a hardmaxxing option for skin laxity, wrinkles and acne scarring. Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure in which sterile needles repeatedly puncture the skin to induce a healing response, also called collagen induction therapy .

name: Secret RF
summary: Cutera's fractional microneedle RF device for skin quality and wrinkles, with two registered studies and little else documented here.
lead: Secret RF is a fractional microneedling radiofrequency device made by Cutera and used in aesthetic medicine for skin quality and facial wrinkles. Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure in which needles puncture the skin to prompt a healing response .

name: Vivace RF microneedling
summary: An RF microneedling aesthetic device; no study found that names Vivace itself.
lead: Vivace is a radiofrequency microneedling device used in aesthetic procedures. No registered trial or published study located for this entry names the Vivace device specifically.

name: Potenza RF
summary: Cynosure's RF microneedling system for wrinkles, scars and pigmentation, documented mainly through small registered studies.
lead: Potenza is a radiofrequency microneedling system from Cynosure, used in aesthetic dermatology for wrinkles, fine lines, scars, stretch marks and pigmentation. Microneedling in general is a cosmetic procedure that punctures the skin with fine needles to induce healing .

name: Sofwave
summary: Needle-free ultrasound skin-lifting system with many registered trials; a 2023 review describes it as FDA-cleared with clinically significant lift results.
lead: Sofwave is an ultrasound-based, non-invasive skin-lifting system used in aesthetic medicine for skin laxity, wrinkles, acne scars and cellulite. A 2023 review describes ultrasound devices as delivering energy to dermal and subdermal tissue to cause thermal injury, leading to collagen remodeling and lifting, and lists Sofwave and Ulthera as FDA-cleared systems with clinically significant results for eyebrow, submental and neck lift and fine-line reduction .

name: Ultherapy Prime
summary: Updated Ultherapy ultrasound lifting device with better imaging; evidence on the Prime model itself is still early-stage.
lead: Ultherapy Prime is an updated version of the Ultherapy system, a noninvasive aesthetic device that uses microfocused ultrasound with real-time visualization (MFU-V) to tighten and lift skin. It is described in the literature as a second-generation system with an advanced processor and improved imaging compared with the original Ultherapy device.

name: Ulthera DeepSEE
summary: Ulthera's imaging-guided ultrasound lifting system for the lower face and under-chin; trial registered, results not summarised in available sources.
lead: The Ulthera DeepSEE system is a microfocused ultrasound with visualization (MFU-V) device from Ulthera, used for noninvasive skin tightening of the lower face and submentum. Its name is tied to the imaging feature that lets the operator see tissue layers during treatment.

name: Doublo HIFU
summary: Korean HIFU skin-tightening device with two small published studies in Asian patients.
lead: Doublo is an intense focused ultrasound (IFUS, also called HIFU) device made by HIRONIC Co. of Seongnam, Korea, used for noninvasive facial and neck skin tightening. Two published studies in Asian patients have examined it.

name: Ultraformer III
summary: Korean HIFU lifting device; published studies are small and mostly cover the related Ultraformer MPT model.
lead: Ultraformer III is a Korean high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) device used for noninvasive facial lifting and skin rejuvenation. Published studies in the sources cited here mainly concern the related Ultraformer MPT model, and are listed as such below.

name: Thermage FLX
summary: In-office monopolar radiofrequency device for non-surgical skin tightening, backed by many small studies but few controlled trials.
lead: Thermage FLX is a monopolar radiofrequency (RF) device used in aesthetic medicine to heat the deeper layers of the skin with the aim of tightening lax skin and reducing wrinkles without surgery. It is the latest generation of the Thermage line, which is described as the first monopolar RF skin-tightening system to receive US FDA clearance, for periorbital (eye-area) use in 2002 .

name: Exilis Ultra / Exilis Elite
summary: BTL's radiofrequency skin-tightening platform; discussed as a non-surgical option, with little device-specific evidence in the sources reviewed.
lead: Exilis is a radiofrequency (RF) skin-tightening device line made by BTL, listed on Wikipedia among commercial RF devices for non-surgical skin tightening . Exilis Ultra and Exilis Elite are later versions of the platform, which is used by clinicians on the face and body.

name: Venus Legacy
summary: Venus Concept's multipolar RF plus pulsed-magnetic-field device for skin tightening and contouring, with thin published evidence.
lead: Venus Legacy is a Venus Concept radiofrequency device for non-surgical skin tightening, wrinkle reduction and body contouring; Wikipedia lists it among commercial RF skin-tightening devices . Grokipedia describes it as a multipolar RF system that adds pulsed electromagnetic fields and pulsed suction, used for laxity, wrinkles, cellulite and mild fat reduction on the face and body .

name: Venus Viva
summary: Nanofractional RF resurfacing device used for acne scars and wrinkles, supported by small uncontrolled studies.
lead: Venus Viva is a nanofractional radiofrequency device marketed for skin resurfacing, including acne scars and wrinkles. Fractional RF delivers thermal energy through multiple micro-pins in a targeted pattern, which is described as shortening recovery compared with surgery or full ablation .

name: Pelleve
summary: Ellman's 4-MHz monopolar RF system for wrinkles and tightening, backed by small uncontrolled studies.
lead: Pellevé is a monopolar radiofrequency wrinkle-treatment system made by Ellman International, operating at 4 MHz . It was one of the RF devices that followed the introduction of Thermage in 2002 .

name: BodyTite
summary: InMode's radiofrequency-assisted liposuction that adds skin tightening to fat removal; evidence is mostly surgeon-reported series.
lead: BodyTite is a radiofrequency-assisted liposuction (RFAL) system made by InMode. A probe placed beneath the skin delivers bipolar radiofrequency energy to liquefy fat and heat the tissue, after which the fat is aspirated; the heating is intended to make the skin contract, addressing laxity that liposuction alone may leave.

name: AccuTite
summary: InMode's small-area radiofrequency-assisted lipolysis tool for jowl and neck tightening; evidence is small studies and surgeon reviews.
lead: AccuTite is a minimally invasive radiofrequency-assisted lipolysis device from InMode, used for small-area skin tightening and fat reduction, typically on the face and neck. Published reports describe it, together with FaceTite, as delivering radiofrequency energy into the subdermal space to target dermal collagen and excess fat with less downtime and lower cost than open procedures such as neck lifts.

name: Vaser liposuction
summary: Ultrasound-assisted liposuction used for body contouring and abs 'etching'; evidence is mostly surgeon case series plus a few small trials.
lead: VASER (vibration amplification of sound energy at resonance) liposuction is a form of ultrasound-assisted liposuction in which a probe delivers ultrasonic energy to fat before it is suctioned out. It is described in the surgical literature as a third-generation ultrasound technique, introduced after earlier ultrasound devices that surgeons reported as bulky and associated with a higher potential for complications.

name: Power-assisted liposuction (PAL)
summary: A motorized, vibrating-cannula version of liposuction; documented in surgical reports but with little head-to-head trial evidence.
lead: Power-assisted liposuction (PAL) is a variant of suction lipectomy in which the cannula is driven by a motor so that it vibrates or reciprocates rapidly while the surgeon moves it through subcutaneous fat. It is one of several liposuction techniques, alongside tumescent, ultrasound-assisted, laser-assisted and water-jet-assisted methods.
claims: A vibrating cannula gives smoother, more precise fat removal than manual liposuction

name: Water-assisted liposuction (BodyJet)
summary: Liposuction using a pressurized fan-shaped water jet; documented mainly for fat harvesting, with thin evidence for contouring outcomes.
lead: Water-assisted liposuction (WAL), also called water-jet-assisted liposuction, is a liposuction technique in which a fan-shaped jet of fluid is delivered through the cannula to loosen fat and infiltrate anesthetic while the fat is aspirated. BodyJet is a commercial system for the method.

name: Tumescent liposuction
summary: Liposuction under local anesthesia using large volumes of dilute lidocaine; the standard technique, with safety data from large surgeon surveys.
lead: Tumescent liposuction is a liposuction technique in which large volumes of dilute lidocaine and epinephrine are infiltrated into subcutaneous fat before fat is aspirated through thin cannulas. The solution numbs the area and constricts blood vessels to reduce bleeding, so the procedure can be done under local anesthesia. It is credited to dermatologist Jeffrey Klein in the 1980s.
